symbols.name: M
symbols.def: Known outcome envelope \(M\), normalized to be at least one.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: Fixed interior bound \(b\) for the histogram outcome means.

symbols.name: mathcal_X
symbols.def: Generic standard Borel covariate space \(\mathcal X\); the explicit histogram subclass is supported on the measurable coordinate interval \([0,1]\subseteq\mathcal X\).

symbols.name: mu_0
symbols.def: Control regression \(\mu_0(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=x]\), with an arbitrary bounded version where the arm is unsupported.

symbols.name: mu_1
symbols.def: Treated regression \(\mu_1(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=x]\), with an arbitrary bounded version where the arm is unsupported.

symbols.name: q_delta
symbols.def: Capped intervention with \(q_\delta(1\mid x)=\min\{1,\delta e(x)\}\) and \(q_\delta(0\mid x)=1-q_\delta(1\mid x)\).

symbols.name: Y_q_delta
symbols.def: Potential outcome \(Y^{q_\delta}\) under a treatment draw from \(q_\delta(\cdot\mid X)\).

symbols.name: w_0
symbols.def: Weight \(w_0(r)=(1-\delta r)/(1-r)\) for \(r<c\) and \(w_0(r)=0\) for \(r\ge c\).

symbols.name: mathcal_M_np
symbols.def: Unrestricted bounded-outcome observational model \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{np}}\) defined in \(\text{def:np-model}\).

symbols.name: mathcal_M_margin
symbols.def: Punctured-margin subclass \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm m}(\alpha,C_{\mathrm m})\) defined in \(\text{def:margin-model}\).

symbols.name: mathcal_M_hist
symbols.def: Explicit cap-crossing histogram benchmark class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{hist}}(b,L)\) defined in \(\text{def:hist-model}\).

symbols.name: B_j
symbols.def: Equal bin \(B_j=[(j-1)/J_n,j/J_n)\), with the last bin closed at one.

symbols.name: Pi_n
symbols.def: All-data conjugate nuisance posterior \(\Pi_n\) defined in \(\text{def:histogram-posterior}\).

symbols.name: H_n
symbols.def: Deterministic truth-centered histogram sieve defined in \(\text{def:posterior-sieve}\).

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: Conditional Bayesian-bootstrap weights \(W=(W_1,\ldots,W_n)\sim\mathrm{Dirichlet}(1,\ldots,1)\), independent of \(\eta\sim\Pi_n\) given the data.

symbols.name: CI_n
symbols.def: Equal-tailed \((1-\gamma)\)-credible interval \(C_n^\gamma\) from the conditional law of \(\Psi_\delta^*\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: One of \(\{e=c,\tau>0\}\) and \(\{e=c,\tau<0\}\) having nonzero contrast integral.

symbols.name: P_t
symbols.def: Two-sided submodel \(P_t\) that keeps \(P_X\) and the outcome conditionals fixed and sets \(e_t=e+t\mathbf 1_B\) for sufficiently small \(|t|\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Fixed shell width \(h\) for the sharpness construction.

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: Boundary distance \(U\) with distribution \(P(U\le t)=(t/h)^\alpha\) for \(0\le t\le h\).

assumptions.condition: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed from \(P\).
The observed outcome satisfies \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\) almost surely.
The pair \((Y_0,Y_1)\) is conditionally independent of \(A\) given \(X\).
For every \(0<t\le c\wedge(1-c)\), \(P\{0<|e(X)-c|\le t\}\le C_{\mathrm m}t^\alpha\).

novel.justification: This is an explicit canonical random-design benchmark with positive density at the cap and both propensity endpoints represented; it is satisfied by a uniformly distributed scalar baseline score.

assumptions.condition: The observational propensity satisfies \(e(x)=x\) for every \(x\in[0,1]\).

novel.justification: The identity propensity is a transparent calibrated-risk benchmark with continuous cap contact and no strong overlap; it includes the practically relevant case in which a scalar assignment score is calibrated to treatment frequency.

assumptions.condition: For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the conditional law of \(Y\) given \(A=a,X=x\) is Bernoulli with mean \(\mu_a(x)\).

novel.justification: Binary endpoints are common for clinical and policy events, and conjugacy makes every posterior coordinate and zero-count fallback explicit.

standard.name: Hölder smoothness of order one for outcome nuisance functions

novel.justification: Event probabilities separated from zero and one describe outcomes with irreducible noise and guarantee a nondegenerate inferential target in the explicit benchmark.

definitions.name: Branchwise residual weights
definitions.construction: \(w_1(r)=\delta\mathbf 1\{r\le c\}+r^{-1}\mathbf 1\{r>c\}\) and \(w_0(r)=\{(1-\delta r)/(1-r)\}\mathbf 1\{r<c\}\), with the displayed branches defining the values at \(r=0,1,c\).

definitions.name: Deterministic equal-bin partition
definitions.construction: Set \(J_n=\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil\) and \(B_j=[(j-1)/J_n,j/J_n)\) for \(j<J_n\), with \(B_{J_n}=[(J_n-1)/J_n,1]\); compute \(N_j\) and \(N_{aj}\) from all \(n\) observations.

definitions.name: All-data Beta histogram posterior
definitions.construction: Independently over bins, assign \(s_j\sim\mathrm{Beta}(1,1)\) and \(u_{aj}\sim\mathrm{Beta}(1,1)\); update \(s_j\) with the \(N_j\) treatment indicators and update \(u_{aj}\) with the \(N_{aj}\) outcomes in arm \(a\), retaining the prior as the total zero-count fallback. Extend each draw constantly on \(B_j\) to obtain \(\eta=(s,u_0,u_1)\sim\Pi_n\).

definitions.name: Branch-relevant deterministic sieve
definitions.construction: For a sufficiently large fixed \(C\), let \(H_n\) be the set of histogram draws satisfying \(\|s-e\|_\infty\le C\rho_n\), \(\|u_0-\mu_0\|_{L_2(P_X)}+\|u_1-\mu_1\|_{L_2(P_X)}\le C\varepsilon_n\), \(\sup_{x\le c+C\rho_n}|u_0(x)-\mu_0(x)|\le C\rho_n\), and \(\sup_{x\ge c-C\rho_n}|u_1(x)-\mu_1(x)|\le C\rho_n\), where \(\rho_n=J_n^{-1}+\sqrt{J_n\log n/n}\) and \(\varepsilon_n=J_n^{-1}+\sqrt{J_n(\log n)^2/n}\).

definitions.name: Bayesian-bootstrap one-step posterior
definitions.construction: Draw \(\eta\sim\Pi_n\) and, conditionally independently given the data, \(W\sim\mathrm{Dirichlet}(1,\ldots,1)\); set \(\Psi_\delta^*=\sum_{i=1}^nW_i m_\eta(O_i)\).

definitions.name: Equal-tailed corrected credible interval
definitions.construction: \(C_n^\gamma=[Q_{\gamma/2}(\Psi_\delta^*\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n),Q_{1-\gamma/2}(\Psi_\delta^*\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)]\), where \(Q_r\) denotes a conditional posterior quantile.

definitions.name: Continuous cap-shell witness
definitions.construction: For \(0<\rho<\min\{h,1-c\}\) and \(h<c\), take \(U\) with \(P(U\le t)=(t/h)^\alpha\) on \([0,h]\), set \(X=U\), \(e(X)=c-U\), draw \(A\mid X\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(e(X))\), and set \(\mu_0=0\), \(\mu_1=1\), and \(Y=A\) under \(P_{\mathrm{lf}}\); set \(s=e+\rho\), \(u_0=\mu_0\), and \(u_1=\mu_1\) in \(\eta_{\mathrm{lf}}\).

definitions.name: Finite-cell conditional-modulus handle
definitions.construction: Start from the legal finite-partition propensity score \(S_B\), derive the Gaussian-threshold limit experiment for \(n^{-1/2}\)-local crossings of \(e=c\), and optimize connected intervals by the conditional modulus while estimating only the active cap cells and the sign of their contrasts.

statements.statement: Under consistency and conditional exchangeability, the causal mean satisfies \(\mathbb E[Y^{q_\delta}]=\Psi_\delta(P)=\mathbb E_P[\mu_0(X)+\tau(X)\min\{1,\delta e(X)\}]\); no strong-overlap condition is required because \(q_\delta(1\mid x)=0\) when \(e(x)=0\) and \(q_\delta(0\mid x)=0\) when \(e(x)=1\).
statements.justification: This fixes the causal interpretation while keeping identification separate from the statistical regularity problem.
statements.gap: Zhou and Opacic identify related interventional effects; this proposition specializes their support-preserving logic to the exact capped mean used below.
statements.consumer: Analysts can interpret every regularity and posterior result as inference for a feasible capped probability-multiplication policy.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{np}}\), the map \(P\mapsto\Psi_\delta(P)\) is pathwise differentiable in the unrestricted observational model if and only if \(K_\delta(P)=0\). At every such regular law its canonical gradient is \(D_P\), its efficiency bound is \(V_P\), and \(D_P\) is uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on \(M\) and \(\delta\). If \(K_\delta(P)>0\), no regular asymptotically linear estimator with an ordinary root-\(n\) Gaussian limit exists at \(P\).
statements.justification: The exact regularity frontier determines when efficient inference is mathematically available and when posterior Gaussian calibration is impossible.
statements.gap: Luedtke and van der Laan characterize an outcome-rule kink; Zhou and Opacic define the capped propensity policy. Neither gives the propensity-kink criterion \(K_\delta(P)=0\) or this positivity-robust canonical gradient.
statements.consumer: A practitioner can diagnose whether an atom in a discrete or heaped assignment score invalidates Wald or Gaussian posterior inference for the capped policy.

statements.statement: Whenever \(K_\delta(P)>0\), one may choose \(B\) so that \(P_t\) is a legal two-sided dominated Bernoulli submodel with bounded finite-partition score \(S_B\), and the two one-sided derivatives of \(\Psi_\delta(P_t)\) at zero are \(0\) and \(\delta\mathbb E_P[\tau(X)\mathbf 1_B(X)]\ne0\). Thus signed cancellation of \(\mathbb E_P[\tau(X)\mathbf 1\{e(X)=c\}]\) cannot restore differentiability.
statements.justification: A legal localized score closes the necessity direction without perturbing binary probabilities outside their support.
statements.gap: Hirano and Porter provide the generic nondifferentiable-experiment implication; the proposed finite-partition tangent embeds that obstruction in the exact binary-treatment cap model.
statements.consumer: The construction supplies a falsification experiment for any claimed regular estimator at an outcome-relevant cap atom.

statements.statement: For every bounded nuisance candidate \(\eta=(s,u_0,u_1)\), including ties \(s=c\) assigned to the saturated branch, the exact identity is \[R(P,\eta)=\delta\mathbb E_P\!\left[\tau(X)|e(X)-c|\mathbf 1\!\left\{\mathbf 1\{s(X)<c\}\ne\mathbf 1\{e(X)<c\}\right\}\right]+\mathbb E_P\!\left[(s(X)-e(X))\left\{\mathbf 1\{s(X)<c\}\frac{(\delta-1)(u_0(X)-\mu_0(X))}{1-s(X)}+\mathbf 1\{s(X)\ge c\}\frac{u_1(X)-\mu_1(X)}{s(X)}\right\}\right].\] Every displayed denominator is bounded away from zero on its active branch. Consequently, if \(\|s-e\|_\infty\le\rho\), the branch-relevant outcome error is at most \(\varepsilon\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm m}(\alpha,C_{\mathrm m})\), then \(|R(P,\eta)|\le C_{\delta,M,C_{\mathrm m}}\{\rho\varepsilon+\rho^{1+\alpha}\}\).
statements.justification: The equality isolates the only nonsmooth bias and gives the rate condition used by both frequentist one-step and posterior corrections.
statements.gap: Kennedy's smooth stochastic-policy remainder has no crossing term, while Levis et al. give a margin upper envelope for different max-min bounds rather than this exact branch-specific identity.
statements.consumer: Posterior and machine-learning users can verify root-\(n\) bias control using only the outcome regression on the branch that is actually observed with stable probability.

statements.statement: For every \(\alpha>0\), \(h<c\), and sufficiently small \(0<\rho<\min\{h,1-c\}\), the construction \((P_{\mathrm{lf}},\eta_{\mathrm{lf}})\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm m}(\alpha,h^{-\alpha})\), satisfies \(\|s-e\|_\infty=\rho\) with the true outcome regressions, and obeys \[R(P_{\mathrm{lf}},\eta_{\mathrm{lf}})=\frac{\delta\alpha}{(\alpha+1)h^\alpha}\rho^{1+\alpha}.\] Hence the exponent \(1+\alpha\) cannot be improved uniformly for this unsmoothed one-step correction over the stated cap-shell class. This is sharpness of the correction modulus, not a minimax lower bound over all estimators.
statements.justification: The equality witness distinguishes a sharp cap-crossing modulus from a merely sufficient margin bound.
statements.gap: Audibert and Tsybakov establish the generic classification exponent; the legal causal witness preserves the capped intervention, treatment law, bounded outcomes, and exact one-step signal.
statements.consumer: Method developers obtain a hard threshold for nuisance rates below which the unsmoothed correction cannot have negligible root-\(n\) bias.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{hist}}(b,L)\), under iid sampling and the all-data Beta histogram posterior with \(J_n=\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil\), a sufficiently large deterministic constant in \(H_n\) gives \(\Pi_n(H_n\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)\to1\) in \(P\)-probability. Moreover, \[\sup_{\eta\in H_n}|\mathbb G_n(m_\eta-m_P)|\to0\] in outer \(P\)-probability. The proof must retain posterior cap crossings, use the minimum expected arm count of order \(n/J_n^2\), and localize changing branches to at most \(2J_n\rho_n+4\) bins. In particular, \(\sqrt n\{\rho_n\varepsilon_n+\rho_n^2\}\to0\).
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing new probability theorem that turns an abstract one-step posterior transfer into an explicit cap-crossing Bayesian procedure.
statements.gap: Castillo controls a single density histogram; Yiu et al. and Schmidt--Wikle require rather than derive this joint unequal-arm contraction and posterior-indexed threshold equicontinuity.
statements.consumer: Users of conjugate Bayesian nuisance models obtain a fully specified, all-data calibration theorem without sample splitting or a no-crossing restriction.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{hist}}(b,L)\), \(K_\delta(P)=0\), \(V_P>0\), and the corrected posterior satisfies \[d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L\!\left(\sqrt n\{\Psi_\delta^*-\mathbb P_nm_P\}\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\right),\mathcal N(0,V_P)\right)\to0\] in \(P\)-probability. Its equal-tailed interval has pointwise frequentist coverage \(P\{\Psi_\delta(P)\in C_n^\gamma\}\to1-\gamma\). The class violates strong overlap because \(e(x)=x\) on \([0,1]\), and posterior draws are not constrained to remain on the true side of the cap.
statements.justification: The theorem delivers efficient Gaussian posterior uncertainty and nominal coverage for the policy-natural hard cap without restoring overlap.
statements.gap: Schmidt and Wikle prove this conclusion for smooth intervention maps; the capped map fails their Taylor and pointwise-Lipschitz steps, which the exact remainder and boundary-bin theorem replace.
statements.consumer: An analysis of capped enrollment, prescribing, or encouragement probabilities can report calibrated posterior intervals even when baseline treatment probabilities approach zero or one.

statements.statement: If \(P\{e(X)=c\}=0\), then \(K_\delta(P)=0\), the regularity theorem applies, and on each of the two fixed branches \(D_P\) equals the ordinary smooth propensity-dependent stochastic-intervention gradient obtained by differentiating \(q_\delta(1\mid x)\) with derivative \(\delta\mathbf 1\{e(x)<c\}\). Thus the result reduces to standard smooth stochastic-policy efficiency theory whenever the cap boundary has no mass.
statements.justification: The reduction checks the new gradient against the established smooth calculation away from the kink.
statements.gap: Kennedy supplies the smooth branch calculation; the proposition records exact agreement rather than claiming that component as new.
statements.consumer: Existing software for smooth stochastic interventions can be validated against the capped formula on datasets with no estimated cap contact.

statements.statement: Does the Gaussian-threshold experiment generated by the finite-partition handle admit a total connected interval with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) uniformly over \(n^{-1/2}\)-local submodels crossing \(e=c\), whose expected length attains the sharp conditional-modulus constant and which reduces to the efficient Wald interval along sequences with vanishing cap signal?
statements.justification: Pointwise regularity and pointwise posterior coverage do not resolve inference for laws drifting toward an outcome-relevant cap atom.
statements.gap: Hirano--Porter and Fang--Santos give generic nonregular limits and bootstrap repairs; neither computes the capped causal tangent cone, sharp interval constant, or adaptation cost.
statements.consumer: Studies with discretized or heaped propensity scores need valid uncertainty statements when cap contact cannot be ruled out from the data.

sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed observational sampling from an unrestricted binary-treatment law; the explicit posterior theorem specializes to \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\) and \(e(x)=x\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with unknown observational propensity \(e(x)\); the intervention uses \(q_\delta(1\mid x)=\min\{1,\delta e(x)\}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Strong overlap is not assumed. The policy preserves observational support, and the histogram benchmark has essential propensity infimum zero and essential supremum one.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All observations update independent Beta histogram coordinates for the propensity and two arm-specific Bernoulli regressions on \(J_n=\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil\) equal bins; independent Dirichlet Bayesian-bootstrap weights perform the one-step correction.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies the intervention \(\min\{1,e^\delta\pi(x)\}\) and develops identification and estimation of its interventional effects.
The optimal-value parameter is pathwise differentiable if and only if its stated exceptional-law variance condition holds.
Smooth incremental propensity-score interventions admit a nonparametric efficient influence function and efficient one-step estimation without positivity.
Uniform no-bias, \(L_2\)-stability, and empirical-process conditions imply a semiparametric one-step posterior Bernstein--von Mises theorem.

For twice continuously differentiable stochastic intervention maps with stable influence functions, the corrected posterior is asymptotically efficient and its credible intervals have pointwise frequentist coverage.
Dirichlet random histograms attain the optimal sup-norm posterior contraction rate for Hölder densities.
A margin condition controls nonsmooth branch selection and permits root-\(n\) influence-function inference for covariate-assisted causal bounds.
The plug-in classification boundary error has the sharp \(1+\alpha\) margin power under sup-norm regression error.
A corrected causal posterior has an efficient Gaussian limit and exact pointwise credible-set coverage under product-rate conditions and strong overlap.
Nondifferentiability in a finite-dimensional local experiment rules out regular locally unbiased estimation.
Ordinary bootstrap validity for a directionally differentiable map requires full differentiability, while a derivative bootstrap can remain valid.

tldr: Multiplying a treatment probability and capping it at one defines a support-preserving intervention but introduces a kink at \(e(X)=1/\delta\). The proposal characterizes the exact pathwise-differentiability frontier by the outcome-relevant cap signal \(K_\delta(P)\), derives the bounded efficient influence function and an exact branch-specific one-step remainder, proves the sharp margin modulus for cap crossings, and establishes efficient one-step posterior Gaussian calibration and pointwise credible-set coverage for an explicit all-data Beta histogram posterior whose draws cross the cap and whose truth violates strong overlap. A legal finite-partition tangent supplies the nonregular converse, while uniform local inference across the regularity boundary remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: The capped probability-multiplication policy is already explicit in the interventional-effects literature, but smooth stochastic-intervention efficiency and posterior theorems cannot differentiate through its interior cap. General one-step posterior theory assumes the exact remainder and empirical-process conditions that cap-crossing draws violate, and existing histogram contraction does not cover joint conditional coordinates with unequal random arm counts.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a complete regularity-and-calibration theory for one identified, positivity-robust stochastic intervention at laws that may touch the cap or the propensity endpoints.
project_justification.fill: The project joins an if-and-only-if regularity theorem, a bounded canonical gradient, an exact crossing remainder with a sharp margin equality example, and a concrete conjugate histogram posterior theorem proved by random-count concentration and boundary-bin localization.

related_work: Zhou and Opacic define and motivate multiplicative propensity interventions capped at one; their results are the policy anchor and do not supply a cap-contact regularity analysis. Kennedy derives efficient influence functions and one-step estimation for smooth incremental odds interventions without positivity, supplying the score calculus on each fixed branch. Luedtke and van der Laan give the closest exact exceptional-law differentiability theorem for an optimal treatment value, but their kink is driven by the outcome contrast and has a different cancellation mechanism. Yiu et al. provide the general Bayesian-bootstrap one-step posterior transfer theorem, whose remainder, stability, and empirical-process obligations are verified here for a nonsmooth target. Schmidt and Wikle verify those obligations for twice continuously differentiable stochastic interventions using Taylor and influence-function Lipschitz arguments; the capped map violates both steps. Castillo's strong contraction theorem motivates conjugate histogram coordinates but concerns a single density rather than conditional treatment and outcome laws with unequal arm counts. Levis et al. and Audibert--Tsybakov supply the credited margin-localization technique and classical \(1+\alpha\) exponent; the proposed novelty is the exact capped causal remainder and its overlap-free branch geometry, not the generic exponent. Breunig, Liu, and Yu provide a smooth causal posterior-coverage benchmark under product rates and strong overlap. Hirano--Porter and Fang--Santos inform the nonregular diagnostic and open local-inference question rather than serving as claims the proposal purports to sharpen.
technical_internal_limitation: The explicit posterior theorem is intentionally proved first on the canonical law \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\), \(e(x)=x\), with Bernoulli Lipschitz outcomes. Its early kill test is \(\delta=2\), \(\mu_0=1/4\), and \(\mu_1=3/4\): the deterministic posterior sieve and uniform corrected-signal empirical-process remainder must be proved while retaining all-data fitting and cap crossings. The bin-count calculation gives minimum expected arm count of order \(n/J_n^2\), and the boundary-bin calculation gives at most \(2J_n\rho_n+4\) uncertain bins, so no strong-overlap or no-crossing repair appears necessary. A simulation cannot substitute for this theorem. SoftBART, simultaneous inference over \(\delta\), and uniform inference over local cap-contact sequences are outside the proved core.
honest_scope: The iff regularity theorem, exact remainder, sharp one-step crossing modulus, explicit histogram concentration and empirical-process theorem, and pointwise posterior coverage are all to be proved. The generic \(1+\alpha\) margin exponent, general one-step posterior transfer, smooth stochastic-intervention theory, and generic nondifferentiable bootstrap theory are credited prior art. The sharp local confidence-interval constant and adaptation across regular and nonregular sequences remain explicitly open. Nonregularity rules out regular asymptotically linear Gaussian inference; it does not rule out every root-\(n\)-length confidence procedure.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 3.1, Assumption 3, Supplementary Sections 8.3, 8.5, and 8.6, and the Introduction and Discussion were read from the arXiv source. The first changed step is the quadratic Taylor bound for the intervention map; the second is pointwise influence-function Lipschitzness used to transfer nuisance brackets.
seed_details.kernel: For \(J_n=\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil\), prove a conditional one-step posterior Bernstein--von Mises theorem and pointwise credible-set coverage for an all-data Beta histogram whose propensity draws cross \(1/\delta\), under the explicit no-strong-overlap benchmark \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\) and \(e(x)=x\).
seed_details.red_team: Objection: Yiu et al. and Castillo immediately imply the result. Rebuttal: Yiu et al. assume the cap-specific posterior remainder and empirical-process conditions, while Castillo treats one density histogram and does not control two unequal random treatment-arm posteriors or a posterior-indexed threshold class.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Sections 1, 3.2, 3.3, and 5 were read from the arXiv source. The paper defines the multiplicative propensity intervention capped at one and discusses estimation, but does not analyze positive-mass contact with the cap.
seed_details.kernel: Prove that the capped intervention mean is pathwise differentiable in the unrestricted observational model if and only if \(K_\delta(P)=0\), derive its canonical gradient, and give a bounded finite-partition propensity tangent witnessing nonregularity when cancellation fails.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is immediate from Luedtke and van der Laan's exceptional-law theorem. Rebuttal: their kink is an outcome-optimal decision and their exceptional condition depends on conditional outcome variance; here the unknown treatment propensity itself crosses the kink, so positive assignment variance at the interior cap yields a different cancellation criterion and tangent.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Section 3, Theorem 2, the proof term controlling branch mistakes, the Introduction, and the Discussion were read from the arXiv source. Their argument supplies an upper margin envelope, not an exact capped-policy identity or a matching causal construction.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the exact two-branch one-step remainder, retain its overlap-free branch denominators, and prove that the crossing component has sharp order \(\rho^{1+\alpha}\) under a punctured propensity-margin condition.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: the rate follows immediately from the standard classification margin inequality. Rebuttal: the exact causal score contains branch-specific outcome errors and denominators; the identity, endpoint conventions, and legal continuous-margin equality example are absent from the classification result.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The Discussion expressly leaves a functional Bernstein--von Mises theorem over an intervention-index set open.
seed_details.kernel: Prove weak convergence of the entire cap-indexed corrected posterior process in \(\ell^\infty([\underline\delta,\overline\delta])\) and simultaneous credible-band coverage with a moving threshold \(1/\delta\).
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this only uniformizes the pointwise theorem. Rebuttal: posterior-indexed moving-boundary tightness is additional mathematics, but it would leave the pointwise cap theorem unresolved and is too broad for the first version.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 2 and its no-bias, \(L_2\), and empirical-process hypotheses were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.kernel: Allow a positive-measure region with \(e=1/\delta\) and \(\tau=0\), and prove a growing-bin corrected posterior Gaussian limit although posterior draws create nonzero contrasts and cross the cap independently across cells.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: contrast cancellation makes this a finite-dimensional delta method. Rebuttal: a growing number of cap cells creates a nonparametric threshold process, but bin alignment narrows the empirical scope relative to the continuous benchmark.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The finite-dimensional nondifferentiable local-experiment argument and the Introduction and conclusion were checked on the publisher record and against the adjacent Fang--Santos and Luedtke--van der Laan constructions.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the capped mean's Gaussian-threshold local experiment and the sharp connected-interval expected-length constant, with an interval adapting between regular and cap-contact sequences.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: generic nondifferentiable-functional theory already supplies the limit experiment. Rebuttal: the weighted conditional-propensity tangent cone is target-specific, but the sharp constant and adaptation step remain too speculative and are retained as the proposal's open-ended question.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Lemma 5.1, Theorem 3.5, the Assouad construction in Section 6.2, and the Introduction were read. Their lower bound concerns classification excess risk, not estimation of the capped causal mean.
seed_details.kernel: Embed the cap shell in a Hölder causal model and match a cross-fitted one-step upper rate by an Assouad minimax lower bound over all estimators.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: higher-order influence-function estimators may improve the one-step nuisance-product term. Rebuttal: a legal lower reduction might rule this out, but no such reduction is yet verified, so the proposal claims only sharpness of the one-step crossing modulus.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The capped multiplicative intervention and its policy interpretation were read in Sections 1 and 3.2; the destination search found smooth individualized odds-policy learning, but no hard-cap margin-regret theorem.
seed_details.kernel: Learn a covariate-indexed multiplier under a treatment-capacity constraint and prove a welfare-regret frontier containing the cap-margin term.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: smooth incremental policy-learning papers already handle resource constraints. Rebuttal: a hard cap changes the uniform score expansion, but optimizing the policy changes the fixed-estimand topic materially.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The bootstrap-validity equivalence and estimated-directional-derivative repair were read from the arXiv source together with the Introduction and conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: At cap-contact laws, estimate the active-cell directional derivative and prove validity of a derivative bootstrap for the non-Gaussian capped plug-in limit.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is a direct application of Fang and Santos. Rebuttal: active-set estimation is nontrivial, but the finite-cell result remains too close to their general theorem for the present paper's kernel.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: A target--method search for conformal or permutation inference for stochastic-intervention means found counterfactual-prediction work but no valid symmetry orbit for this observational mean.
seed_details.kernel: Invert a permutation or conformal test to obtain finite-sample intervals for the capped stochastic-intervention mean.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: permuting treatment is invalid when \(e(X)\) varies, while permuting observed triples yields no missing-potential-outcome orbit. Rebuttal: none exists without changing to a randomized design or sharp null, so the seed is dropped rather than padded.

literature_map.settled: The multiplicative propensity intervention capped at one is explicitly defined and causally motivated.
literature_map.open_boundary: Regularity at positive mass on the interior cap and its canonical gradient are not treated.

literature_map.settled: Smooth incremental odds interventions have identified means, efficient influence functions, and one-step estimators without positivity.
literature_map.open_boundary: The hard cap invalidates the smooth chain rule at \(e=1/\delta\).

literature_map.settled: An exact pathwise-differentiability frontier is known for the value of an optimal treatment rule.
literature_map.open_boundary: Its outcome-decision exceptional set and conditional-variance cancellation differ from a propensity kink with positive treatment variance.

literature_map.settled: A general corrected-posterior Bernstein--von Mises transfer theorem reduces calibration to remainder, \(L_2\), and empirical-process conditions.
literature_map.open_boundary: Those conditions are assumed rather than verified for cap-crossing nuisance draws.

literature_map.settled: A pointwise corrected-posterior theorem is proved for twice continuously differentiable intervention maps using Taylor and pointwise-Lipschitz arguments.
literature_map.open_boundary: The capped map is outside those hypotheses and needs a different remainder and entropy argument.

literature_map.settled: Dirichlet random histograms attain optimal sup-norm density contraction under Hölder regularity.
literature_map.open_boundary: No joint conditional Beta result under unequal random treatment-arm counts or cap-threshold empirical process is given.

literature_map.settled: A margin condition yields root-\(n\) inference for nonsmooth causal bound endpoints through a branch-disagreement upper bound.
literature_map.open_boundary: The exact capped-policy remainder, overlap-free branch denominators, and equality construction are absent.

literature_map.settled: The \(1+\alpha\) plug-in boundary power and matching classification lower constructions are classical.
literature_map.open_boundary: This proposal credits that exponent and adapts only the causal branch identity and legal capped-policy equality example.

literature_map.settled: Efficient pointwise posterior coverage is available for smooth causal targets under product rates and strong overlap.
literature_map.open_boundary: The all-data hard-cap target without strong overlap is not covered.

literature_map.settled: Ordinary bootstrap validity is characterized and an estimated-directional-derivative bootstrap is provided for directionally differentiable maps.
literature_map.open_boundary: The result informs the open local-inference question but is not claimed as a new generic bootstrap theorem.

literature_checklist.author: Xiang Zhou and Aleksei Opacic
literature_checklist.one_line: Sections 1, 3.2, 3.3, and 5 define the capped multiplicative intervention and its estimands but do not study cap-contact regularity.

literature_checklist.author: Tyler M. Schmidt and Nathan B. Wikle
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 3.1 and Supplementary Sections 8.3, 8.5, and 8.6 use bounded second derivatives and pointwise influence-function Lipschitzness that the hard cap lacks.

literature_checklist.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 gives an iff exceptional-law differentiability criterion for an optimal value and constructs unequal one-sided derivatives.

literature_checklist.author: Edward H. Kennedy
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 2, Corollary 2, and the appendix remainder lemmas give the smooth propensity-dependent intervention score and nuisance-product cancellation.

literature_checklist.author: Andrew Yiu, Edwin Fong, Chris Holmes, and Judith Rousseau
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 2 reduces one-step posterior calibration to uniform no-bias, influence-function stability, and empirical-process conditions.

literature_checklist.author: Ismaël Castillo
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 3 proves optimal sup-norm contraction for Dirichlet random histograms under Hölder smoothness.

literature_checklist.author: Alexander W. Levis, Matteo Bonvini, Zhenghao Zeng, Luke Keele, and Edward H. Kennedy
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B
literature_checklist.one_line: The nonsmooth-bound theorem and its proof localize branch-selection error under a margin condition but provide an upper envelope rather than the capped identity.

literature_checklist.author: Jean-Yves Audibert and Alexandre B. Tsybakov
literature_checklist.one_line: Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 3.5 establish the classical plug-in margin power and matching classification lower rates.

literature_checklist.author: Christoph Breunig, Ruixuan Liu, and Zhengfei Yu
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 give efficient posterior limits and pointwise coverage for smooth causal effects under product rates and strong overlap.

literature_checklist.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter
literature_checklist.one_line: The finite-dimensional local experiment translates nondifferentiability into regular-estimation impossibility.
